articles.title: Yosemite Star Party
articles.summary: The Yosemite Star Party at Glacier Point offered clear observing nights where participants engaged in various astronomical activities. Lew successfully observed Pluto, while the author experimented with CCD imaging for public viewing, capturing an image of Comet Linear. The event also featured constellation and trivia contests, as well as the presentation of AANC and FPOA astronomy awards.

articles.title: Annual Star-B-Que Report
articles.summary: The annual FPOA/AANC Star-B-Que was held on July 29th, featuring sizzling food, numerous telescopes (around 50-60), and various competitions including an Astronomical Gastronomical contest and a Create-a-Constellation challenge for young people. Despite initial cloudy conditions, attendees enjoyed observing through telescopes and binoculars, a presentation on the NASA Multi-instrument Aircraft Campaign for the Leonid Storm, and notable sightings of Comet Linear and asteroid Vesta.

articles.title: Shallow Sky: Watch a Triple Transit on Jupiter
articles.summary: This article highlights a rare triple transit event on Jupiter occurring on September 6 at 12:35 a.m., involving Io, its shadow, and Europa's shadow. It also provides a monthly observing guide, detailing the visibility of other planets like Jupiter and Saturn (now rising earlier for telescopic viewing), Venus, Mercury, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, and Mars, noting their positions and phases.

articles.title: Meteors
articles.summary: This article provides a guide to September meteor showers, emphasizing the month's good sporadic rates and minor showers like the Alpha and Delta Aquarids. It also features an observing report from August 12th, detailing a successful viewing session of Perseid meteors, fireballs, the Andromeda galaxy, and planetary alignments despite a bright moon.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: The article explores the Moon's formation and prominent surface features, particularly its maria and multi-ring impact basins like Mare Orientale and Mare Nectaris, encouraging observers to view these "scars of evolution" and understand the physics of high-energy impacts. It details observing tips for these features, including specific dates in September. Separately, the article announces the naming of asteroid (10683) Carter after Carter Worth Roberts, recognizing his long-standing contributions to the Eastbay Astronomical Society and astronomy.

articles.title: December Holiday Party
articles.summary: The club's December general meeting will be held as a holiday party and social occasion on December 9th at 8 pm. Attendees are encouraged to bring food/drink contributions, items for a "show and tell" display, and an anonymously wrapped astronomical item for a "white elephant" gift exchange, promising a fun-filled evening.

articles.title: Astronomy Magazine Renewal Time
articles.summary: This announcement details the renewal process for Astronomy magazine subscriptions for the year 2001, offering a group rate of $29. Subscribers can renew existing group subscriptions, convert independent subscriptions to the group rate, or start new subscriptions by sending payment and details to Jim Van Nuland. Contact information for questions is also provided.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The article details the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner telescope program, providing lists of scopes currently available for immediate borrowing, those on loan with due dates, and those on extended loan. It also mentions a waiting list for popular scopes and recent activities involving a newly acquired Orion XT6 Dobsonian telescope. SJAA members can contact Mike Koop to borrow a scope.
